name: Paraiso 2011
question: Does robotic assistance change operative time and recovery compared with conventional laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy for posthysterectomy apical prolapse?

design.population: Seventy-eight women aged at least 21 years with posthysterectomy POP-Q stage 2–4 vaginal apex prolapse who desired laparoscopic repair were randomized at the Cleveland Clinic.
design.locator: Materials and Methods, eligibility and randomization paragraphs; Results, first paragraph

verdictNote: The prespecified operative-time comparison was significant, with robotic surgery slower.
takeaway: Robotic-assisted versus conventional laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy prolonged the prespecified incision-to-closure operative time by 66 minutes in women with posthysterectomy apical prolapse; robotic surgery also had greater postoperative pain and health-system cost.

reports.label: Primary randomized report
reports.dateLocator: Crossref published-print: November 2011; PubMed journal issue: November 2011
reports.citation: Paraiso MFR, Jelovsek JE, Frick A, et al. "Laparoscopic compared with robotic sacrocolpopexy for vaginal prolapse: a randomized controlled trial." *Obstet Gynecol.* 2011;118(5):1005-1013. doi:10.1097/AOG.0b013e318231537c
reports.followUp: Six weeks for pain and cost; one year for support and functional outcomes
reports.followUpLocator: Materials and Methods, outcome-assessment and cost paragraphs

results.measure: Mean incision-to-skin-closure time; robotic minus laparoscopic mean difference in minutes
results.note: Prespecified two-sided test for a difference, which favored conventional laparoscopy; 35 robotic and 33 laparoscopic patients underwent surgery.

results.measure: Robotic minus laparoscopic mean difference in suturing time, minutes
Pain at rest and during normal activities at postoperative weeks 3–5
results.note: The full-text narrative reports significant differences without a pooled numeric estimate.
results.locator: Results, six-week postoperative pain paragraph; Figure 3

results.measure: Mean surgery, hospitalization and related care cost through six weeks, 2011 US dollars; robotic minus laparoscopic mean difference
results.note: The analysis excluded robot purchase and maintenance and patient or societal costs.
results.locator: Results, cost paragraph; Materials and Methods, cost paragraph

results.measure: Between-group anatomic support and quality-of-life comparisons at one year
results.note: No between-group difference was reported; the trial was not powered for small differences in long-term anatomic or functional outcomes.
results.locator: Results, anatomic and quality-of-life paragraph; Discussion, limitations paragraph

harms.label: Conversion to another operative approach
harms.note: Robotic: one laparotomy after two cystotomies and sigmoid injury, two laparoscopies for robot malfunction. Laparoscopic: one laparotomy and one vaginal conversion.

harms.label: Overall intraoperative and postoperative complications
harms.note: The narrative reports no difference; a graded complication distribution was not provided.

delivery.label: Surgical team and mesh
delivery.value: Two attending urogynecologic surgeons, assisted by fellows, used two separate 4×15-cm polypropylene mesh pieces; both attendings had performed at least 10 robotic-assisted procedures.
delivery.locator: Materials and Methods, surgical-team and laparoscopic-technique paragraph

delivery.label: Laparoscopic access and suturing
delivery.value: Four ports: 5-mm umbilical, two 10/12-mm lower-quadrant, and one 5-mm subcostal; extracorporeal knots.
delivery.locator: Materials and Methods, laparoscopic-technique paragraph; Figure 1 legend

delivery.label: Robotic access and suturing
delivery.value: Five ports in a shallow W: 12-mm umbilical, 12-mm right subcostal, and three 8-mm lower-quadrant ports; cart docked between the legs; intracorporeal knots.
delivery.locator: Materials and Methods, robotic-technique paragraph; Figure 1 legend

delivery.label: Concomitant procedures
delivery.note: Procedures were performed at the primary surgeon's discretion.
